questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2} \\  & {x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=-\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(\frac{1}{2})+(-1)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+1+1=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=4$, ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨4,\frac{1}{2},-1⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\  & {x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & {x}_{3}=3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=3.$ Substitute this into the second equation to get

$$
{x}_{2}-(3)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-1+3=2.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-(2)+(3)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1-3+2=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=0$,  ${x}_{2}=2$, and ${x}_{3}=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨0,2,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y-z=4 \\  & y+2z=2 \\  & z=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
he third equation states that  $z=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+2(\frac{1}{2})=2\,⟹\,y=2-1=1.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=\frac{1}{2}$ and $y=1$ into the first equation to get

$$
x-(1)-(\frac{1}{2})=4\,⟹\,x=4+1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{11}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\frac{11}{2}$,  $y=1$, and $z=\frac{1}{2}.$  In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨\frac{11}{2},1,\frac{1}{2}⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=3 \\  & {x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-6(-\frac{1}{3})=3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3-2=1.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+1-(-\frac{1}{3})=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2-1-\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}$, ${x}_{2}=1$, and ${x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as
$[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ 1 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=9 \\  & {x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that  ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-3(\frac{1}{3})=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2+1=3.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-(3)+3(\frac{1}{3})=9\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=9+3-1=11.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨11,3,\frac{1}{3}⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say,  ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=5 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\  & {x}_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(2)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-3(-2)+4(2)=5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=5-6-8=-9.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=-9$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨-9,-2,2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say,  ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-2 \\  & {x}_{3}=-3\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that  ${x}_{3}=-3.$ Substituting this into the second equation,  we get

$$
{x}_{2}+2(-3)=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2-2(-3)=-2+6=4.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+2(4)+3(-3)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1-8+9=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=0$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=-3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as
$[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+3z=-2 \\  & y+4z=0 \\  & z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=3.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+4(3)=0\,⟹\,y=-12.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=3$ and $y=-12$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(-12)+3(3)=-2\,⟹\,x=-2+12-9=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$, $y=-12$, and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨1,-12,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say,  ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{2}+\frac{{x}_{3}}{3}=-1 \\  & {x}_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+\frac{2}{3}=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-1-\frac{2}{3}=-\frac{5}{3}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{3}$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+3(-\frac{5}{3})+(2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+5-2=5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=5$, ${x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{3}$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨5,-\frac{5}{3},2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=1 \\  & y+z=1 \\  & z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(1)=1\,⟹\,y=1-1=0.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=1$ and $y=0$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(0)+(1)=1\,⟹\,x=1-1=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=0$, $y=0$, and $z=1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨0,0,1⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=7 \\  & 2{x}_{3}=4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that 

$$
2{x}_{3}=4\,⟹\,{x}_{3}=2.
$$

 Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-{x}_{2}+3(2)=7\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=6-7=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+5(-1)+(2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1+5-2=2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is 
${x}_{1}=2$, ${x}_{2}=-1$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$  In vector form, the solution can be written as $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+y-z=2 \\  & y+3z=6 \\  & -z=-3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that

$$
-z=-3\,⟹\,z=3.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+3(3)=6\,⟹\,y=6-9=-3.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=3$ and $y=-3$ into the first equation to get 

$$
2x+(-3)-(3)=2\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}(2+3+3)=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4$, $y=-3$ and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨4,-3,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 4x+y+2z=-3 \\  & y+3z=0 \\  & -z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that 

$$
-z=1\,⟹\,z=-1.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+3(-1)=0\,⟹\,y=3.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=-1$ and $y=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
4x+(3)+2(-1)=-3\,⟹\,x=\frac{-3-3+2}{4}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1$, $y=3$, and $z=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as 
$[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-3 \\  & -{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that 

$$
-{x}_{3}=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{3}=1.
$$

 Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+2(1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-3-2=-5.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=-5$ into the first equation to get

$$
2{x}_{1}-(-5)+4(1)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{-1-5-4}{2}=-5.
$$

Therefore, the solution is 
${x}_{1}=-5$, ${x}_{2}=-5$, and ${x}_{3}=1.$  In vector form, the solution can be written as $[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+y+z=-1 \\  & y+z=1 \\  & 2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that
 

$$
2z=1\,⟹\,z=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(\frac{1}{2})=1\,⟹\,y=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=y=\frac{1}{2}$  into the first equation to get

$$
2x+(\frac{1}{2})+(\frac{1}{2})=-1\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}(-1-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2})=-1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1$, $y=\frac{1}{2}$, and $z=\frac{1}{2}.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨-1,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}⟩.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The third equation states that $z=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(2)=2 
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad

$$

Now, we substitute both $z=2$ and $y=0$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(0)+(2)=3
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x = 3-2 = 1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x = 1,$ $y=0,$ and $z = 2.$ Or, in vector form, the solution is $\langle 1,0,2 \rangle.$

	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
